why: The agent changes CL-2 from absence to presence after human approval, leaving the version_hash unchanged. IR-11 compares stored version identifiers but does not independently verify that the draft content matches its hash, so RL-1 appears to authorize the opposite conclusion from the one the human reviewed. The unsupported presence claim also bypasses IR-08.

O-6 now claims that the system learned an observation on May 1 even though the observed activity did not occur until May 18. C2 requires meaningful event and learned times, but IR-07 checks learned-time ordering only for derived records, not whether a source observation was supposedly learned before its underlying event occurred.

A source observation for April, already learned before Q-2's cutoff, exists in the store, yet Q-2 still reports complete coverage and zero results. IR-06 constrains records that were returned but does not require a complete query to return all eligible observations; IR-08 therefore accepts an absence claim despite the omitted matching record.

The human release is explicitly scoped to tenant T2, while CL-1 concerns tenant T1 and its released item M-1 is subsequently consumed in a T1 investigation. C3's human authorization cannot legitimately cover promotion and reuse outside the approved scope, but IR-11 through IR-13 never verify that a release's scope includes the conclusion or its downstream use.

RL-1.scope: fraud investigations of tenant T2 only

why: O-5 is an independently authored human note based solely on source observation O-1, despite being written while DR-1 happened to be open. C3 requires provenance links for records actually informed by agent output, not every independent record written during an exposure. IR-14 nevertheless rejects this history because it treats overlapping exposure as sufficient proof of dependence.
